newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs bruised by BOJ rate comments.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs bruised by BOJ rate comments.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures were weak but off their lows in late Wednesday trade after a sharp sell-off earlier on comments by a Japanese official, which triggered fears of a rate rise.

Bank of Japan (BOJ) deputy governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted as saying the central bank was considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate but it did not want to make a hasty decision.

He allegedly made the comment at a meeting with executives of Japan's largest grouping of labour unions, the Japanese Trade Union Confederation (Rengo), at which the labour group urged the BOJ to raise the discount rate.
Reports of the remark sparked large-lot sales, pushing December Euroyen to a low of 98.86 and June JGBs down as far as 123.18 in hectic trade.

Both contracts firmed slightly after other BOJ officials said the central bank would continue to place emphasis on ensuring Japan's economic recovery and that there were no plans for an immediate rate rise.
A senior BOJ official also said Fukui had been wrongly quoted and there was no change in its monetary policy stance.

But the denial did not prompt a full-blown recovery. December Euroyen was quoted at 98.91 at 0910 GMT after trading in a volatile 98.86-98.99 range. Volume was an active 33,250 lots despite a public holiday in Singapore.
June JGBs stood at 123.55 against their previous 124.45.
"The market reacted more to the bad news of course. People seem to be quite long because the sell-off on Euroyen was quite drastic," a trader with a U.S. futures house said.
He said December Euroyen's failure to break above the 99.00 resistance level despite repeated attempts recently had also frustrated participants, who were now pushing it the other way.
"I'm still looking to buy the December but I'd want it to get down to maybe 98.80," he said.
Earlier, Japanese and U.S. interest rate futures were both boosted by the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to hold short-term rates steady at its meeting on Tuesday.
Eurodollars remained firm in late trade but dealers said further upside looked limited as most players believed the Fed had merely deferred a rate hike.
"We saw some new buyers coming in in the morning. We might trade a couple of ticks higher but people are banking on a rate hike at the next meeting," a trader at a European house said.
The most active December contract was at 93.760 at 0910 GMT against its IMM close at 93.735 on volume of 10,615 lots. September was at 93.975 against 93.955.
